title: IPC admin.trust.set params
description: Allow one peer on the data plane, or revoke it (2.1). `allowed: true` adds it, refused `InvalidArgument` for this profile's own identity or for a new peer once the allowlist holds 4096; `allowed: false` removes it, closes every connection it holds at once, drops its cached endpoint directory, and every connection with `events` sees `peer.disconnected` with `reason_class: policy` (ADR-0012); from the Stage 22 release it does these only when the write removes the peer from the admission set, and none of them while another set holds the peer (ADR-0067 decision 6, A 2026-11-19). Adding a listed peer and removing an unlisted one are no-ops answered `ok` (from 2.10 `trust-set-result`'s `set`); from 2.10 a set from an admin connection admitted before the one whose set for the same peer was last applied is refused `superseded`, nothing written. A PERSISTED OVERLAY since ADR-0028 A 2026-10-07: a set that changes the policy is written to the state directory's trust overlay before it is published and answered, so it survives a restart; config.yaml is still never written; every set is written to the daemon's audit log. THE ENDPOINT DIMENSION (IPC 3.0, ADR-0067 decision 6, LOCAL-IPC.md §The endpoint dimension): with an `endpoint`, the set writes the peer into, or out of, BOTH members of that endpoint's own set in the endpoint overlay and never the operator's list; the alias is not accepted, a client resolves it; an `endpoint` outside the grammar is `InvalidArgument`, and an id no configured entry holds is `EndpointUnknown`. Absent, the operator's list as before.
